Surrogates and intended parents attend routine blood testing, counselling, and clinic appointments before treatment.
Donors and intended parents must meet the clinic eligibility criteria and complete the required consent forms.
Donor conception separates genetic contribution, gestation, and day-to-day social parenthood among different people.
A known donor supplies the genetic role while the intended parents replace that contribution with the social and caregiving parent roles.
A parental order grants the intended parents legal parenthood and recognition on the child's birth certificate.
The parental order transfers legal parenthood from the surrogate to the intended parents, separating gestational and legally recognized parent roles.
